s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic skin lesions with atrophic and scar-like appearance on the face
salient_findings: Round atrophic lesions on the face with a diameter of 5 to 10 mm
Lesions located symmetrically and bilaterally on the malar and preauricular areas
Histopathologic examination showing epidermal dell and superficial dermal lymphocytic infiltrate
key_facts: 26-year-old man with a several-year history of persistent skin lesions
Previous diagnosis and treatment were unsuccessful
No history of chicken pox, acne, or traumatic lesions in the affected areas
Lesions are not indurated and display no epidermal changes
Histopathologic examination shows dermal fibrosis
Orcein stain demonstrates reduction of elastic fibers in the dermis
Lesions have a cicatricial appearance
Symmetrical and bilateral distribution of lesions on the face

shortlist.label: Atrophoderma of Pasini and Pierini
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the description of atrophic lesions with a scar-like appearance and symmetrical distribution on the face

shortlist.label: Discoid lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by chronic skin lesions with scarring, which aligns with the patient's presentation

shortlist.label: Lymphocytic infiltrate of Jessner
shortlist.why_kept: Presents with atrophic lesions and a lymphocytic infiltrate, consistent with the patient's histopathologic examination

shortlist.label: Granuloma faciale
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause atrophic lesions on the face, although the histopathology typically shows granulomatous inflammation

shortlist.label: Scleroderma
shortlist.why_kept: Can present with atrophic lesions and dermal fibrosis, but the absence of other systemic symptoms makes it less likely

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of persistent, round, atrophic lesions with a scar-like appearance, symmetrical and bilateral distribution on the face, and histopathologic findings of epidermal dell, superficial dermal lymphocytic infiltrate, and reduction of elastic fibers in the dermis are characteristic of Atrophoderma of Pasini and Pierini.

rejected.label: Discoid lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: Typically presents with indurated, erythematous plaques and epidermal changes, which are not seen in this patient

rejected.label: Lymphocytic infiltrate of Jessner
rejected.why: Usually presents with erythematous, indurated plaques, which are not consistent with the patient's atrophic lesions

rejected.label: Granuloma faciale
rejected.why: Characterized by brownish plaques with a granulomatous infiltrate, which is not seen in this patient

rejected.label: Scleroderma
rejected.why: Typically presents with sclerotic, indurated skin, which is not consistent with the patient's atrophic lesions
